name: The Estée Lauder Companies Inc.
moat_justification: Prestige brand portfolio built over decades (La Mer, Estée Lauder, MAC, Le Labo, Jo Malone London) with genuine premium pricing power, global distribution and FY2026 China share gains, but eroding: three years of revenue decline FY23-25 while L'Oréal kept growing, repeated acquired-brand impairments (Dr.Jart+, Too Faced, Tom Ford), department-store and Asia travel-retail channel decay, and faster local/digital-native rivals.
fragility_flags: OE_VOLATILE: OE/share range over the last 5 yrs spans >3x — normalized base helps but the business is cyclical; widen bear weight
NI_OCF_DIVERGENCE: net income and operating cash flow differ by >40% in 2024, 2025, 2026 — find the one-off (tax deposits, impairments, WC swings) before trusting the OE base
one_liner: Real prestige-brand moat (5/10) in a genuine early turnaround, but at $102.29 the price capitalizes the recovery in advance against trough-normalized owner's earnings of $2.76/share — weighted IV@15% is $23.52 (IRR 5.43%, Tier D); it only clears the 15% hurdle at ~$23.52, or ~$19 with a margin of safety.
moat_for: Prestige brand portfolio built over decades (La Mer, Estée Lauder, MAC, Le Labo, Jo Malone London) with genuine premium pricing power
Global prestige distribution plus a record 34% of sales online in FY2026
Mainland China prestige share gains in FY2026 (China sales +9%) and fragrance +10%
Scale in R&D and marketing that sub-scale rivals cannot match
moat_against: Three straight years of revenue decline (FY2023-25) while L'Oréal kept growing
Repeated nine-figure impairments on acquired brands (Dr.Jart+, Too Faced, Tom Ford)
Structural channel decay in US department stores and Asia travel retail
Rising local Chinese brands and digital-native indies move at TikTok speed
Lauder-family dual-class control limits outside discipline on capital allocation
